findings.title: Plain GLB changes equal-column lookup even on sorted nonnegative maps
findings.claim_challenged: whole-map TraceMap GLB + units/raw-index projection and remapping
findings.finding: Pinned lookup advances through every eligible segment and picks the last exact duplicate generated column. traceSegment and originalPositionFor use GREATEST_LOWER_BOUND, but an exact match is moved through lowerBound to the first duplicate. remapping recursively calls traceSegment, so an unmodified original map can change composition too. This gap remains after excluding negative, unsorted and overflow maps.

evidence.note: Source-order scan keeps last eligible segment.
Finite profile explicitly names last duplicate and observable mutable maps.
traceSegment uses GLB.
GLB exact hit invokes lowerBound.
upperBound walks forward; lowerBound walks backward over equal columns.
Composition uses traceSegment on child maps.
Existing effectiveLine coalesces equal thresholds to the last point before composition.

findings.recommended_assessment_wording: Full-map APIs are conditionally viable after qualifying input domain, exact-column tie behavior, raw source/name indexes, coordinate units and failure containment. Ordinary sorted maps with duplicate columns still require a small tie bridge/coalescing step or an explicitly selected different caller profile; units and raw-index projection alone are insufficient.

wrapper_judgment.necessary_now: Preserve current finite last-duplicate behavior while comparison promises same outcomes. A narrow coalescing/tie policy bridge can be materially smaller than the existing full compatibility mechanics.
wrapper_judgment.avoidable_if_qualified: Large overflow carriers and prefix-maximum transforms for unsorted maps need not become permanent requirements merely because the old oracle includes them.
wrapper_judgment.not_claimed: No implementation, runtime counterexample execution or generated-map duplicate inventory.

findings.owner_JEV: A factual assessment correction does not select policy. Owner/JEV is required if changing supported tie behavior or narrowing legitimate callers; this review does not make that choice.

findings.assessment: adapters / csv-export-stringify / required_outcomes, options_limitations, necessary_wrapper; inherited AD-export-csv-bytes
findings.title: Current CSV export uses LF, not CRLF
findings.claim_challenged: CRLF trailing terminator; fixed CRLF/eof options preserve current byte profile
findings.finding: At the semantic pin pageToCsv explicitly returns lines joined with LF plus one trailing LF. The finite C04 handoff retains that serializer and supplies no CRLF selection. The contract record and fit assessment both say current CRLF, which conflicts with their source authority. csv-stringify with record_delimiter CRLF would alter every record boundary compared with the pinned mechanics.

evidence.note: Header and armored/escaped data rows use lines.join(LF) plus LF.
Retain existing tiny serializer and separate formula neutralization.
With eof=true the supplied record_delimiter is appended.

findings.recommended_assessment_wording: The current source profile uses LF record separators and a trailing LF. For a same-byte stringify candidate use LF with eof=true, keep owner formula armor, and force quotes for any comma, quote, LF or CR. CRLF is a different output profile that would need explicit selection if desired.

wrapper_judgment.necessary_now: Projection, current grants, exact selected row/header ordering, owner formula protection, fixed LF/eof and quoting options.
wrapper_judgment.avoidable: A second custom quoting scanner alongside stringify.
wrapper_judgment.tradeoff: The existing quote helper is tiny; retaining it remains a fair alternative and avoids a dependency without lowering product outcomes.

findings.owner_JEV: Correcting the observed LF description requires no new policy. Selecting CRLF instead would be an owner choice, with affected output consumers qualified. No output change is authorized here.

findings.title: Separate trace-map internal caching from mutation of caller-owned decoded arrays
findings.claim_challenged: TraceMap resolves raw names and caches/mutates sorted input domain
findings.finding: TraceMap retains raw sources/names and constructs resolvedSources. For unsorted decoded mappings supplied as an object, maybeSort shallow-copies the outer array and copies unsorted lines before sorting. It mutates arrays parsed from its own JSON input, not these caller-owned unsorted lines. Internal decoded caches and sharing of already-sorted input still require a mutation/invalidation-domain qualification, but the broad mutation claim overstates the actual implementation.

evidence.note: Raw tables are retained, resolved sources derived, ownership flag comes from JSON-string parsing.
Non-owned outer/unsorted inner arrays are copied before sorting.
Encoded and decoded forms are cached internally.

findings.recommended_assessment_wording: TraceMap derives resolvedSources and caches decoded mappings. Caller-supplied decoded unsorted lines are copied for sorting, while sorted input/table references may be shared. Cross-call map mutation and raw-identity handling need their own finite qualification; do not attribute arbitrary input mutation to the library.
findings.owner_JEV: Evidence wording correction only. A new cache lifetime or narrowed mutation domain would be a separate owner decision.

seam_reviews.verification: Pinned replay.ts hashes sorted raw data before receipt lookup and validation (admission.ts:321,323,342,366). evidence.note: Buffer::format handles nonfinite text and delegates finite numbers.
f64 nonfinite masks select NaN or signed Infinity.
Both positive and negative zero return 0 before sign is emitted.
Current explicit String branches and separate JSON nonfinite-null channel.
Values diagnostics use String policy.

seam_reviews.same_outcome_comparison: String route: Buffer::format(n).to_owned() preserves source-observed zero/nonfinite behavior. JSON route must still emit null for nonfinite and finite JS numeric text otherwise. format_finite alone is unsuitable for an unrestricted String input; neither formatter admits approximate Number as exact Can int/decimal.
seam_reviews.wrapper_judgment: String allocation/error integration and JSON-channel policy are necessary. Separate zero/NaN/Infinity branches are redundant with Buffer::format. No decimal/exponent rewrite or second numeric engine is needed.
seam_reviews.policy_choices: No policy choice is needed for mechanical removal of redundant branches after qualification. Changing persisted Work bytes or diagnostic promises would be separate owner work; no change implemented.
